feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid evidence of scope across web, content, analytics, and multimedia. It reads well overall, but impact would improve with sharper outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression align well with digital strategy/communications leadership.  
- Good credibility signals: recognized employers, internal promotion history, and concrete scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).  
- Broad but coherent skill set: combines strategy, CMS/web execution, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that fits mission-driven organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: include results such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, production savings, adoption rates, or campaign impact.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve scannability.  
- Minor writing/style issues: use “12 years of experience” (missing “of”); standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2)”. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding a clearer leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your seniority and niche: digital strategy/communications leadership for mission-driven or advocacy-focused organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a sharper value statement tied to transformation, governance, and audience engagement.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial workflow design, analytics, and digital governance across web, email, social, and multimedia platforms. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused content and aligning stakeholders around effective advocacy and communications strategies.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” are also reinforced elsewhere, so keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership areas will make it more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform administration,” “Editorial operations & governance,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Prioritize strategic, senior-level strengths over generic tasks; consider: “Digital strategy & platform transformation • Editorial operations & governance • Web platform & CMS management • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow systems design • Stakeholder alignment • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia production & live events”
- Replace “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” with a more executive phrase like “Stakeholder alignment” or “Cross-functional leadership.”
- Consider changing “Web & CMS administration” to “Web platform & CMS management” for a stronger, more modern tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “policy & advocacy communication,” and coordination language repeat the header and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a broad responsibility list rather than a high-impact engagement. Tighten it around 3–4 outcomes and distinguish it from the NACo roles by emphasizing consulting, platform delivery, and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with the client, scope, and value: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and communications operations.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-led line: “Built cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make delivery bullets more concrete: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable outcomes if possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, teams enabled, publishing time reduced, search success improved, or engagement gains from the AI-enabled search work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps heavily with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version more execution- and consulting-focused.
- The microsite and AI search bullets also echo Recent Projects, so avoid repeating the same feature details verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale signals; it should be tightened to emphasize executive ownership and clearer outcomes. Focus this entry on enterprise leadership and transformation, not routine channel management already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for enterprise communications.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific or measurable: include email list size, engagement growth, social growth, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available.
- Tighten phrasing like “expanded analytics infrastructure” to “implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting stack, improving leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects and earlier NACo video bullets; stress scale, capability-building, or budget impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later NACo director role and the earlier digital media role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what was built or scaled before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging prior to promotion to Director of Digital Media.”
- Tighten bullets to concrete responsibilities: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video impact: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role; keep this entry centered on execution and scaling.
- “Produced weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; here, stress expansion/standardization rather than initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership areas not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-oriented wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & UX
- Consider dropping “audience-focused” for “audience strategy” or “content strategy” to sound more senior.
- Keep wording parallel: noun-based phrases or “X & Y” constructions throughout.
- If space allows, prioritize “web modernization” and “content operations,” which are strongest in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also echoed in Core Competencies; rephrase if this section should add new value.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize current strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the most relevant/recent items first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, then implementation/integrations.
- Consider dropping older or less-evidenced platforms here unless central to target roles; keep this section focused on strongest differentiators.
- If space allows, use “content systems” or “digital platforms” language to align with leadership positioning, not just hands-on execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” are already covered in “Technical + IT”; repeating all three here weakens impact.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also appear in Core Competencies; keep wording distinct or consolidate.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads more like a tool dump than a senior, impact-oriented topline category. Reframe it around strategic analytics leadership, with tools secondary.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics Strategy, Reporting & Optimization
- Rewrite as: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis
- Put the strategic items first if space allows: KPI framework design, executive reporting, performance optimization, then tools
- If you can support it elsewhere, add outcome language indirectly through framing: analytics infrastructure, decision support, and optimization rather than just platform names

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep this version strategic and leave the other as the detailed tools list
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; avoid repeating both phrases verbatim

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and several NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and make it feel more senior than task-based.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic tools/tasks with outcome-oriented capabilities: “Broadcast-quality studio production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Video editing and post-production”
- Consider adding scale/scope if true: “for advocacy programming, conferences, and recurring executive content”
- Use parallel noun phrases rather than mixed verbs/nouns; avoid “video production and editing” if “studio production” and “post-production” cover it more cleanly
- If multimedia is not a target priority, shorten to 3–4 terms to preserve space for stronger digital/platform leadership skills

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; use different wording here or remove one instance
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already evidenced in recent NACo experience, so don’t over-list near-synonyms

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened or reframed to emphasize depth in the most relevant platforms, especially Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by relevance/recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal (10, enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider renaming to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want more impact, swap the weakest item for a stronger capability already evidenced in experience, e.g., “Drupal • CMS modernization • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; keep one version shorter or more platform-specific.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise/public-sector focus unless it supports a notable project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, not repeat broader skills.

Suggested edit
- Reframe as applied technical capabilities: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider replacing older/basic labels like “HTML5” and “CSS3” with “Front-end implementation” for a more senior tone.
- If accurate, add specificity tied to recent work: “Drupal front-end customization,” “analytics/tag deployment,” or “workflow/deployment automation.”
- Order by relevance/recency: JavaScript, API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, Google Tag Manager, then jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; either remove them there or make this section more tool-specific.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap with analytics infrastructure; keep it here only if positioned as implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and overlaps with “Workflow automation” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize automation/integration tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Integration & Work Management Tools
- Reorder by relevance/impact: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana
- Move Slack, Teams, and possibly Basecamp/Trello out unless the role specifically required administering workflows in them; they read as generic collaboration tools.
- If space allows, add a qualifier for stronger positioning: “Airtable workflow design • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana project operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; this section should list tools only, not repeat the concept.
- Airtable is already called out in Topline Skills (“Airtable systems”); keep the wording here concise to avoid echoing it.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for this profile, but the item is too bare and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these were hands-on systems you actively managed; otherwise remove any tool used lightly.
- If space allows, add a short qualifier for impact: **Enterprise newsletter and member-engagement platforms supporting high-volume advocacy and stakeholder communications**
- Order by strongest/recentest platform experience first; if Higher Logic was the main NACo system, list it before Dynamics/Mailchimp.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets about newsletters/email; keep this item tool-specific and avoid repeating channel ownership.
- If Dynamics 365 was not central to recent roles, consider dropping it to keep the technical stack aligned with your strongest, most recent experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer scope and outcomes: “Supported a major website refresh, improved cross-channel publishing workflows, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Tighten leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- If available, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or workflow efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; here, frame it as launching or early production rather than expansion.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/program support and the “first podcast” milestone.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Tighten generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer action, e.g., “produced digital and multimedia content supporting member communications and policy initiatives.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a two-part structure: one clause on innovation/research coordination, one on podcast/digital production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/media leadership here; that progression is better shown in the 2015–2024 entries.
